title: 9 best new K-dramas to watch in November 2026 - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao October 29, 2026 November is bringing another exciting line-up of K-dramas, with fresh stories and familiar faces returning to our screens. From star-studded fantasy romances and gripping crime thrillers to heartwarming comedies and historical epics, there's plenty to look forward to this month. Highlights include Shin Min-a's highly anticipated "The Remarried Empress," the return of fan favourites "Good Partner" and "Crash," and Park Min-young's latest office romance. Whether you're in the mood for something lighthearted or a little more intense, here are nine new K-dramas worth adding to your watchlist this November 
 The Remarried Empress (November 4)
 One of November's most anticipated releases, The Remarried Empress brings the popular web novel and webtoon to life with a star-studded cast. Shin Min-a plays Navier, the empress of the Eastern Empire, whose marriage falls apart when her husband, Emperor Sovieshu (Ju Ji-hoon), takes runaway slave Rashta (Lee Se-young) as his mistress and demands a divorce. But rather than giving up her position, Navier turns the tables by requesting to remarry Prince Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk) of the Western Empire, setting the stage for a dramatic power struggle filled with romance and betrayal.
 One of a Kind Romance (November 9)
 Red Velvet's Joy teams up with Kim Hyun-jin in One of a Kind Romance , a romantic comedy adapted from the popular webtoon of the same name. Joy plays Gong Yu-il, a struggling job seeker who crosses paths with top actor Tak Mu-i (Kim Hyun-jin), only for him to mistake her for a stalker. Things take an unexpected turn when she ends up becoming his manager, and he discovers she's actually the author of a novel that once helped him through a difficult time. As they get to know each other, their rocky relationship slowly blossoms into something more.
 Happy Anding (November 11)
 For something a little more heartfelt, Happy Anding follows three struggling comedians, played by Kang Hoon, Cho Hyun-chul and Kim Jung-jin, who have spent a decade chasing their dreams without much success. Adapted from the Japanese drama Life's Punchline , the story takes a turn when they cross paths with Go Eun-young (Lee Yi-dam), a devoted fan who has withdrawn from the outside world, and her free-spirited younger sister. As new relationships develop, the trio begins to reconsider their futures in this heartwarming story about friendship, love and finding a fresh start.

 What a Boss Wants (November 11)
 Sung Hoon and Oh Se-young lead What a Boss Wants , a romantic comedy that puts a musical twist on the familiar CEO love story. Sung Hoon plays Kwon Do-hyuk, a cold and calculating entertainment CEO who finds comfort in the voice of a mysterious indie singer. He soon discovers she's Lee Eun-chae (Oh Se-young), a struggling job seeker who secretly performs under the name Soo. When he offers her a three-month contract to work as his secretary, the arrangement brings them closer than either expected, and romance soon enters the picture.
 Sword & Silence (November 14)
 Historical drama fans have something to look forward to with Sword & Silence , a 28-episode epic starring Lee Hyun-wook, Jang Hyuk, Kim Kang-woo and Park Sung-woong. Set during Korea's Three Kingdoms period, the story follows Kim Beop-min (Lee Hyun-wook), the future King Munmu of Silla, who struggles to understand his father Kim Chun-chu's (Kim Kang-woo) diplomatic decisions. But as war breaks out, he joins forces with legendary general Kim Yu-sin (Park Sung-woong) to take on rival kingdoms and China's Tang dynasty, all in the hopes of unifying the peninsula.
 Crash 2: Fury Road (November 16)
 The Traffic Crime Investigation team is back for more high-speed action in Crash 2: Fury Road . Lee Min-ki, Kwak Sun-young and Heo Sung-tae reprise their roles, while NCT's Jisung joins the team as rookie officer Ji Dae-se. Now operating under the National Office of Investigation, the team takes on even more dangerous traffic crimes across the country. When a series of road explosions turns out to be deliberate murders rather than accidents, the investigators find themselves chasing a much bigger case, bringing another entertaining mix of action, crime and comedy.
 Good Partner 2 (November 20)
 After winning over viewers with its gripping divorce cases and workplace drama, Good Partner is back for a second season. Jang Nara returns as Cha Eun-kyung, a veteran divorce lawyer who has now established her own law firm, Rebom. This time, she crosses paths with Kang Hye-sung (Kim Hye-yoon), an ambitious lawyer whose passionate approach to cases clashes with Eun-kyung's more rational mindset. After initially facing off in court, the two must learn to work together as they navigate complicated divorces and help their clients move forward with their lives.
 The Blue Road (November 20)
 If you're in the mood for something darker, The Blue Road brings together Son Suk-ku and Japanese actor Eita Nagayama in an eight-episode crime thriller. Set across South Korea and Japan, the story follows Seoul detective Kim Seok (Son Suk-ku) and Tokyo detective Inose (Eita Nagayama), who join forces after a string of gruesome murders leaves behind mysterious messages written in Korean and Japanese. Despite their different approaches to solving crimes, the pair must put their differences aside to track down the killer. With D.P. director Han Jun-hee behind the camera, this looks like one for thriller fans.
 Nine to Six (November 25)
 Park Min-young returns alongside BTOB's Yook Sungjae and Go Soo in Nine to Six , a workplace romance adapted from the Chinese drama The Rational Life . Park plays Kang Yi-ji, a career-driven deputy manager at an automobile company who has little time for love. But her carefully organised life begins to change when she meets warm-hearted intern Han Seon-woo (Yook Sungjae). With office politics, career pressures and a demanding boss played by Go Soo adding to the mix, Yi-ji finds herself reconsidering her priorities as an unexpected romance begins to blossom.
